text: Big Brother 5 is the fifth season of the American reality television series Big Brother, based on the Dutch series that gained prominence in 1999 and 2000. It premiered on CBS on July 6, 2004, and concluded on September 21, 2004, after eleven weeks and 82 days. The season featured 14 HouseGuests, an increase from prior seasons, and included a total prize of $500,000 for the winner and $50,000 for the Runner-Up. The season introduced the spin-off series House Calls: The Big Brother Talk Show, an online webshow hosted by Gretchen Massey and Marcellas Reynolds, which aired thirty-minute episodes on weeknights and allowed fan calls and interviews with evicted HouseGuests, making it the first live Internet talk show produced exclusively for a television network. The season aired on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, a shift from the previous season’s Wednesday and Friday schedule. The Thursday episode at 8 p.m. Eastern Time featured the live eviction and Head of Household competition, hosted by Julie Chen, while the Saturday episode at 9 p.m. included the food competition, nomination ceremony, and highlights. The Tuesday episode featured the Power of Veto competition and ceremony. The season premiere, which aired on Tuesday at 8 p.m. due to a conflict with The Amazing Race 5, lasted ninety minutes and drew 9.55 million viewers, nearly matching the previous season’s premiere and ranking as the third highest-rated premiere in the series’ history. Ratings remained steady, with the finale attracting over 10 million viewers. The format included weekly challenges, Head of Household competitions, and Power of Veto competitions, with the Head of Household immune from nominations and responsible for nominating two HouseGuests. The winner of the Power of Veto could save one nominee from eviction, requiring the Head of Household to nominate a replacement if the power was exercised. Evictions were decided by a vote of the HouseGuests, excluding the Head of Household and nominees, with a final message allowed for nominees before voting in the Diary Room; in case of a tie, the Head of Household broke it. The jury, consisting of the last seven evictees, voted on the winner during the finale and were sequestered, not allowed to view Diary Room interviews or strategy-related footage. The season’s theme was "Project Do Not Assume" or "Project DNA," featuring two major twists: Michael "Cowboy" Ellis and Jennifer "Nakomis" Dedmon were revealed to be half-siblings with the same father, a fact that Ellis discovered and which Big Brother later confirmed with letters from home; and twins Adria and Natalie switched spots in the house, successfully completing the task and with Natalie entering on Day 35, a twist later used in Big Brother 17. This season also introduced a Fast Forward Week, where two HouseGuests were evicted in one week with concurrent Head of Household and Power of Veto competitions, and it was the first season in which only six players participated in the Power of Veto competition: the Head of Household, the two nominees, and three others selected by the three. The house remained largely unchanged, with a one-story structure, two-way mirrors, and cameras throughout, including a swimming pool and hot tub, with the fish tank now featuring miniature sharks. The bedrooms included a room with four stone beds (called "pretty bad" by Julie Chen), one with three beds and no privacy, one with two large beds requiring two HouseGuests to share, and the Head of Household room, which introduced a spy screen showing other rooms. The season began with 13 original HouseGuests entering on Day 1, who competed in the "Hungry Hungry Helix" food challenge, where Lori won a "lobster tail" ball and accepted a $10,000 offer to put the house on peanut butter and jelly diet. On Day 2, Drew, Jase, Michael, and Scott formed the "Four Horsemen" alliance, while Karen, Lori, and Will formed a separate alliance. Michael discovered Nakomis was his sister but chose not to reveal it. On Day 3, the "Treadmills of Terror" Head of Household competition was held, with Jase and Scott as finalists, and Jase winning after correctly answering a tie-breaker. Michael later revealed the sibling twist to Jase and Scott, who convinced him to tell Nakomis, and the twist was revealed to all HouseGuests that night. On Day 4, the "Margarita Madness" luxury competition was held, where the group won the hot tub and a margarita party. On Day 6, Jase nominated Mike and Nakomis, targeting Mike. On Day 8, the Power of Veto competition, "Flaringo Toss," was held, with Scott winning the power. On Day 10, Jase left nominations unchanged. On Day 14, Mike was evicted in a 10-to-0 vote. The "Majority Rules" Head of Household competition followed, with Marvin winning after correctly answering a tie-breaker. On Day 15, the "Catapoultry" food competition took place, where Will landed a chicken in the "bad egg" space, resulting in a loss of food, but the group still gained some. Marvin then nominated Holly and Lori. Lori’s allies secured five votes to keep her in the game. For the Power of Veto, Drew chose Scott, Holly chose Jase, and Lori chose Karen. In the "Snag the Veto" competition, Jase narrowly beat Lori to win the Power of Veto. On Day 18, Jase used the Power of Veto on Holly, replacing her with Karen. On Day 21, Lori was evicted in a 7-to-2 vote. The "High/Low" Head of Household competition was held on Day 22, won by Drew. On the same day, Drew nominated Holly and Nakomis, causing a rift in the Four Horsemen. For the Power of Veto, Drew chose Scott, Holly chose Jase, and Nakomis chose Natalie (pretending to be Adria). In the "Bluff Me a Veto" competition, each player acted as a dealer, drawing a card with a question and truthful answer, reading the question and either giving the truth or bluffing, with HouseGuests deciding whether the person was truthful. Drew Daniel was crowned the winner, and Michael Ellis was named the Runner-Up. Holly King appeared on Big Brother 6 to host a Power of Veto competition, and Diane Henry, Jennifer "Nakomis" Dedmon, and Jase Wirey returned to Big Brother: All-Stars in 2006. Michael "Cowboy" Ellis was a candidate for All-Stars but did not return, while Marvin Latimer and Scott Long also returned. Jase appeared on Big Brother 10 in a food competition and was a candidate for Big Brother 11 in 2009 but did not enter. Jase was one of four international alumni up for a public vote in Big Brother Canada’s fourth season but was not selected.

On Day 22, HouseGuests participated in the "Alphabet Soup" food competition, where they had to leap into a giant bowl of tomato-flavored Alphabet Soup and grab letters to spell a type of food, with the group winning the foods they spelled for the week. That same day, Drew nominated Holly and Nakomis for eviction, which created a rift in the Four Horsemen alliance. In the Power of Veto competition, Drew chose Scott, Holly chose Jase, and Nakomis chose Natalie (pretending to be Adria). Each player acted as a "dealer," drawing a question and answer from a questionnaire, reading the question to the others, and either revealing the truthful answer or bluffing a different one; HouseGuests then bet with a chip labeled "Bluff" or "Truth" to decide if the dealer was truthful or not. The dealer kept their chip if the HouseGuest was wrong, and the player with the most chips after two rounds won. Nakomis won the Power of Veto. On Day 25, Nakomis used the Power of Veto on herself, with Adria named the replacement nominee. On Day 28, Holly was evicted in a vote of seven to one. The following day, HouseGuests competed in the "I Have a Secret" endurance Head of Household competition, where they stood on a pedestal with a life-size cutout of themselves, holding a finger over a button on the cutout without crossing a black line; if they removed their hand, they were eliminated. Diane won after nearly nine hours, becoming the first female Head of Household of the season. No food competition was held that week. On Day 29, Diane nominated Jase and Scott for eviction. For the Power of Veto, Diane chose Will, Jase chose Michael, and Scott chose Drew. In the "This Little Piggy Won the Veto" competition, each player had ten Veto chips to distribute into six ceramic pigs representing HouseGuests, with the pig closest to 20 chips without exceeding it winning. Jase won the competition and later removed himself from the block, with Marvin becoming the replacement nominee. On Day 35, Scott was evicted in a vote of four to three. The twins twist was revealed, and Natalie entered the house as an official HouseGuest. After Scott's eviction, HouseGuests competed in the "Home Is Where the Answer Is" Head of Household competition, where they answered true or false questions about the house; if incorrect, they were eliminated, and Nakomis won. On Day 36, HouseGuests competed in the "Fast Times and Custard Pie" food competition, where they ate disgusting pies to find an "eat" card for food for the week. Adria, Diane, Jase, and Drew were on the peanut butter and jelly diet. Nakomis developed the "Six Finger Plan," intending to nominate two allies, and during the Veto competition, she and her allies would choose three others to ensure a team member won the Veto. She hoped to nominate Jase as the replacement nominee so he could not play for the Veto. On Day 36, Nakomis nominated Diane and Marvin for eviction. For the Power of Veto, Nakomis chose Adria, Marvin chose Will, and Diane chose Drew. In the "Pop Goes the Veto" competition, HouseGuests threw darts at a wheel of balloons with HouseGuest faces behind them; when all of a player’s balloons were popped, they were eliminated. Drew won the Power of Veto. Drew then removed Diane from the block, with Jase becoming the replacement nominee. On Day 42, Jase was evicted in a vote of six to one. After Jase's eviction, HouseGuests competed in "The Puck Stops Here" Head of Household competition, where they shot a puck down a shuffleboard with rubber bands attached, aiming for a blue space; Adria was closest and became the new Head of Household. On Day 43, HouseGuests competed in the "Backyard Burger Bonanza" food competition, splitting into two teams of four to assemble hamburgers; the team with the most hamburgers won food for the week. Diane, Drew, Marvin, and Natalie were on the peanut butter and jelly diet, making it the second consecutive week Drew and Diane were on the diet. That day, Adria nominated Marvin and Will for eviction. For the Power of Veto, Adria chose Drew, Will chose Diane, and Marvin chose Michael. In the "A Very Veto Christmas" competition, HouseGuests traded Christmas presents worth Veto points; the player with the highest total won. Adria won the Veto. The HouseGuests later participated in the "Admit One" luxury competition, where Diane, Drew, and Will earned the right to watch the comedy film Without A Paddle. Adria left the nominations intact. On Day 49, Will was evicted in a vote where Adria broke the tie, becoming the first member of the Jury of Seven. After Will's eviction, HouseGuests competed in "Who Said It?" Head of Household competition, where they answered questions based on statements from previously evicted HouseGuests; if incorrect, they were eliminated, and Nakomis won for the second time. On Day 50, HouseGuests competed in the "Smoothies from hell" food competition, where they blended their favorite meals and drank them; if successful, they earned food for the day they represented. They earned food for every day of the week except Saturday. That day, Nakomis nominated Adria and Natalie due to Adria's betrayal the previous week. The HouseGuests later participated in "The Web" luxury competition, where Diane won a $1,000 online shopping spree. For the Power of Veto, Nakomis chose Marvin, Adria chose Drew, and Natalie chose Michael. In the "Mug Shot" Power of Veto competition, the faces of three HouseGuests were combined into one picture, and the HouseGuest who correctly identified the three individuals in each of six pictures won. Adria won the Power of Veto for the second consecutive week and used it to save herself, with Nakomis nominating Michael in her place. On Day 56, Natalie was evicted in a vote of four to one, becoming the second member of the Jury of Seven. After Natalie's eviction, HouseGuests competed in "Putting for Power" Head of Household competition, where they split into two groups of three and attempted to get a ball into a hole on an uphill course; the first from each group to succeed advanced to a final round, where the person who sank the most balls in sixty seconds won. Marvin advanced and won, becoming Head of Household for the second time. On Day 57, Marvin nominated Adria and Michael for eviction. For the Power of Veto, Marvin chose Drew, Adria chose Karen, and Michael chose Nakomis. In the "Ice Ice Veto" competition, HouseGuests used a "Super Soaker Gun" to free a Veto medallion from a frozen block of ice, with a "T" allowing them to open a toolbox; the first to free the medallion won. Karen won the Power of Veto, securing her first win of the season. Karen later decided to keep Adria and Michael nominated. On Day 63, Adria was evicted in a unanimous vote of four to zero, becoming the third member of the Jury of Seven. After Adria's eviction, HouseGuests competed in the "Chemical Reaction" Head of Household competition, where they answered questions about past events by pouring chemicals into a container; correct answers turned the chemical blue, and Drew won, making it his second time holding the title. The HouseGuests learned it would be a Double Eviction week, with an eviction occurring the following day. That night, Drew nominated Diane and Marvin for eviction. On Day 65, HouseGuests competed in the "Bounced" Power of Veto competition, where they attempted to bounce balls into a hoop in the fastest time; Diane won. She used the Power of Veto to save herself, with Nakomis becoming the replacement nominee. That same night, Marvin was evicted in a unanimous vote of three to zero, becoming the fourth member of the Jury of Seven. After Marvin's eviction, HouseGuests competed in the "Ready, Set, Gone" Head of Household competition, where they answered questions about missing items; Nakomis won, becoming the first person this season to hold the title three times. On Day 65, Nakomis nominated Drew and Michael for eviction. On Day 66, HouseGuests competed in the "Caged" Power of Veto competition, where they built a device to get keys to unlock a cage; Diane won, marking her second consecutive Power of Veto win. Diane used the Veto on Drew, with Karen being the only eligible nominee in his place. On Day 70, Karen was evicted in a unanimous vote of two to zero, becoming the fifth member of the Jury of Seven. After Karen's eviction, HouseGuests competed in the "Before or After" Head of Household competition, where they were asked whether events happened before or after each other; Drew won, making it his third title. On Day 71, HouseGuests competed in the "Trashin' the Fashion" luxury competition, where they earned a shopping spree by destroying disliked clothing. That day, Drew nominated Diane and Nakomis for eviction. The HouseGuests later competed in the "Socket to Me" final Power of Veto competition, where there were ten boxes with images of the Head of Household, nominees, and Veto winner; they had to electrically link all Veto winners in order, and the fastest completed the task won. Michael won, securing his first Power of Veto win of the season. On Day 75, Michael used the Veto to save a nominee, evicting the other nominee not saved; he chose to use the Veto on Diane. With Drew (HoH), Michael (Veto winner), and Diane (Vetoed) all immune, Nakomis was evicted by Michael’s sole vote, becoming the sixth member of the Jury of Seven. After Nakomis' eviction, HouseGuests competed in the "Earthquake" first round of the final Head of Household competition, where they held onto keys while standing on a moving platform; Drew won. Diane and Michael later competed in the "Twisted Twosomes" Head of Household competition, which Michael won. On Day 78, Drew and Michael competed in the "Encore Presentation" Head of Household competition; Drew won, becoming the final Head of Household of the season. Moments later, he cast the sole vote to evict Diane. On Day 82, the Jury of Seven voted to award Drew the grand prize in a vote of four to three. Big Brother 5 averaged 8.30 million viewers per episode. The season premiere drew 9.55 million viewers, finishing first in its time slot for total viewers and key demographics. The Thursday, July 15 episode, which saw Mike being evicted, had 8.76 million viewers, up 12% from the previous episode and won its time period for total viewers and all key demographics. The Tuesday, August 3 episode, featuring Jase winning the Power of Veto, had 9.7 million viewers and averaged 8.98 million, winning all time periods. The Thursday, August 12 episode, featuring Jase's eviction, had ten million viewers. The Tuesday, August 17 episode came in third, behind the Olympics, with 8.2 million viewers. The Tuesday, August 24 episode averaged 9.6 million viewers. The Tuesday, September 7 episode averaged 10.7 million viewers, with a strong 6.8 Nielsen rating and 11 share. The Thursday, September 9 episode had a 6.2 rating and 10 share. The finale had 10.54 million viewers, the highest-rated episode of the season.
